illuminate.config.title: Illuminate
illuminate.config.enabled.tooltip: Control your lights from Minecraft. When off, your lights go back to their own software.
illuminate.config.saturation.tooltip: How colorful your lights are. Values above 100% make the game's soft colors stand out more on LEDs.
illuminate.config.smoothing.tooltip: How slowly the room fades when you move between biomes, caves and the time of day. Flashes stay instant.
illuminate.config.frame_rate.tooltip: How often the lights update. Lower it if your devices lag behind.
illuminate.config.reduce_flashing.toolti: Makes damage, lightning and explosion flashes softer and slower. Turning on the game's Hide Lightning Flashes setting also softens lightning.
illuminate.config.dim_in_menus.tooltip: Dims your lights while the pause menu, your inventory or another screen is open in a world.
illuminate.config.idle_mode.tooltip: What your lights do on the title screen and in other menus outside a world.
illuminate.config.idle_mode.release.tool: Illuminate stops controlling your lights until you join a world. OpenRGB devices go back to their own mode and the SignalRGB effect turns dark.
illuminate.config.show_preview.tooltip: Shows what your lights display in the top left corner of the screen. The left of the preview is your left, the top is the sky.
illuminate.config.show_virtual_room.tool: Shows a small desk setup in the top right corner, lit live by Illuminate: a monitor with a glow behind it, light bars, an LED strip and a PC case. Handy for showing the mod without your own room. It stays visible when you hide the HUD with F1.
illuminate.config.log_events.tooltip: Writes every damage, explosion, lightning strike and other event to the game log.
illuminate.config.f3_entry: Illuminate can show its frame rate, connections, colors and the last event on the F3 screen. Press F3 + F6 and turn on the illuminate entry.
illuminate.config.test_command: Play any effect with /illuminate debug, like /illuminate debug damage left or /illuminate debug totem. Nothing in the world happens, only the lights react.
illuminate.config.environment.tooltip: Every biome has its own feel: sun falling through jungle leaves, heat over the desert, glinting snow, rippling water or drifting cherry petals. Daylight sets how bright it is, dawn, dusk and the moon glow on their side and caves take the warm light of torches. The Nether and End use their own colors.
illuminate.config.portals.tooltip: A purple swirl that builds up while you stand in a Nether portal.
illuminate.config.weather.tooltip: Rain drops, snowflakes, Nether embers and End motes drifting through the room.
illuminate.config.submerged.tooltip: Shimmering water, glowing lava and powder snow when your head is inside them.
illuminate.config.status_effects.tooltip: Tints the room in the colors of your status effects. Night vision brightens, blindness and darkness dim and nausea shifts the colors.
illuminate.config.boss_bars.tooltip: Tints the sky in the color of the boss bar while one is shown.
illuminate.config.low_health.tooltip: A red heartbeat that speeds up as your health runs low.
illuminate.config.hazards.tooltip: Flames while you burn, frost creeping in while you freeze and a blue pulse as you run out of air.
illuminate.config.sleep.tooltip: Fades the lights out as you fall asleep in a bed.
illuminate.config.damage.tooltip: A flash when you take damage, colored by what hurt you and brighter on the side the hit came from.
illuminate.config.world_events.tooltip: Flashes for lightning and explosions near you, a burst for a totem of undying and sparkles when you level up.
illuminate.config.fireworks.tooltip: Fireworks burst in their own colors on the side and height they explode at, fading into their fade colors.
illuminate.config.event_intensity.toolti: How strong damage flashes and world events are.
illuminate.config.group.live_preview.too: Your lights, live. The left is your left, the top is the sky. Play an effect to see how it looks.
illuminate.preview.off: Your lights are released to your RGB software
illuminate.config.signalrgb.tooltip: Sends the lighting to the Illuminate effect in SignalRGB. Arrange your devices on the SignalRGB canvas: its left is your left, its top is the sky. You can use OpenRGB at the same time, as long as each device is controlled by only one of them.
illuminate.config.overlap: SignalRGB and OpenRGB are both on. That works when they control different devices. A device controlled by both flickers, so turn it off in SignalRGB or set it to Off under OpenRGB Device Positions.
illuminate.config.signalrgb_apply_effect: Switches SignalRGB to the Illuminate effect when Minecraft starts sending lighting.
illuminate.config.signalrgb_effect.toolt: Copies the Illuminate effect to %s. Restart SignalRGB afterwards to see it.
illuminate.config.signalrgb_port.tooltip: Port of SignalRGB's canvas API. Only change it if SignalRGB uses a different one.
illuminate.config.openrgb.tooltip: Controls the devices of an OpenRGB SDK server directly. Start the server in OpenRGB's SDK Server tab. You can use SignalRGB at the same time, as long as each device is controlled by only one of them. Set devices that SignalRGB controls to Off under OpenRGB Device Positions.
illuminate.config.openrgb_host.tooltip: Address of the OpenRGB SDK server. Use 127.0.0.1 when it runs on this computer.
illuminate.config.openrgb_port.tooltip: Port of the OpenRGB SDK server.
illuminate.config.group.placements.toolt: Where each device sits in your room. Devices appear here after OpenRGB connected once.
illuminate.config.placement.tooltip: Where this device sits in your room, which decides the part of the scene it shows.
illuminate.config.placement.left.tooltip: On your left, from the sky down to the ground.
illuminate.config.placement.center.toolt: In front of you, from the sky down to the ground.
illuminate.config.placement.right.toolti: On your right, from the sky down to the ground.
illuminate.config.placement.above.toolti: Above you, from your left to your right.
illuminate.config.placement.below.toolti: Below you, from your left to your right.
illuminate.config.placement.surround.too: Across the whole room, from your left to your right.
One color blended from the whole room.
illuminate.toast.overlap.title: SignalRGB and OpenRGB are both in use
illuminate.toast.overlap: A device controlled by both will flicker. Turn it off in one of them.
illuminate.toast.effect_installed: Effect installed. Restart SignalRGB to use it.
